facts: BTC Map (btcmap.org) is a community-sourced, open-data map of Bitcoin-accepting merchants worldwide.
MotoPass integrates BTC Map via the v4 REST API (api.btcmap.org) to show merchant density per jurisdiction.
Each MotoPass program has a lat/lon coordinate and radius — the API searches within that circle for Bitcoin-accepting places.
Merchant density is scored into three tiers: sparse (0-4), moderate (5-19), dense (20+) — shown as colored badges on program cards.
The density score is merchants-per-km² scaled to 0-100 — higher means more Bitcoin commerce relative to jurisdiction size.
BTC Map data is pre-fetched daily by fetch-btcmap-density.mjs and cached in public/data/btcmap-density.json for instant client-side display.
Per-jurisdiction snapshots (places + areas) are synced by sync-btcmap-cache.mjs to public/data/btcmap/{slug}.json for offline use.
The BTC Map page (/btcmap) shows an interactive Leaflet map with merchant pins, a searchable directory, category filters, and CSV export.
Merchant categories include: ATM, Store, Restaurant, Cafe, Hotel, Exchange, Medical, Tech, Grocery, Fitness, Bar, Spa, and more (20+ types).
Grid clustering groups nearby pins at low zoom levels — cell size scales from 0.45° (zoom ≤7) to 0.045° (zoom ≥11).
BTC Map authentication uses NIP-98 (Nostr HTTP Auth) — sign in with a Nostr extension to save favorite merchants across devices.
Saved merchants are persisted in localStorage (motopass-btcmap-saved) with a future Nostr kind-event sync for cross-device.
Cache freshness is tracked: fresh (≤7 days), recent (8-14 days), expired (>14 days) — stale caches show a warning banner.
The intel pipeline uses BTC Map as a signal source — merchant count feeds into crypto_friendly_score for each country.
BTC Map places have: id, lat, lon, name, icon (category), address, verified_at (community verification date), website.
Each merchant links to btcmap.org/merchant/{id} for community-maintained details and verification status.
Google Maps directions links are generated from merchant coordinates — deep-link to turn-by-turn navigation.
The 'Report Venue' feature links to btcmap.org/add-location with pre-filled coordinates and program name.
CSV export downloads the merchant directory as a portable spreadsheet with program name, id, name, address, coordinates, and verification date.
BTC Map is open data — attribution to btcmap.org, OpenStreetMap, and the btcmap-api GitHub repo is required on all views.
The BTC Map page supports three layout modes on tablet: split (map + directory), map-only, and list-only.
Jurisdiction jump lets users quickly switch between programs with BTC Map data without returning to the dropdown.
Lightning-ready badges on merchant pins indicate Lightning Network payment support (tags.payment.lightning === 'yes').
The BTC Map embed uses Leaflet with OpenStreetMap tiles — no Google Maps API key required.
Offline cache staleness is detected by comparing fetchedAt against the current date — expired caches show a red banner.
Merchant search is debounced (280ms) and filters by name and address — results highlight matching text.
Virtual scrolling is used for directories with 48+ merchants — only visible rows are rendered for performance.

places_search.returns: BtcMapPlace[] — id, lat, lon, name, icon, address, verified_at, website

areas_at.returns: BtcMapArea[] — id, name, type, url_alias, icon, website_url

cache_system.density: public/data/btcmap-density.json — per-program merchant count + tier + score
cache_system.snapshots: public/data/btcmap/{slug}.json — full place list + areas per jurisdiction
cache_system.manifest: public/data/btcmap/manifest.json — list of all synced programs with file names and counts

honesty_rules: BTC Map data is community-sourced — merchant counts may lag behind real-world changes.
A merchant pin on BTC Map does not mean the venue definitely accepts Bitcoin today — verify before visiting.
Density tiers are approximate — a jurisdiction with 19 merchants (moderate) is not dramatically different from 20 (dense).
Cache staleness is honest — if the data is 10+ days old, tell the member and suggest checking btcmap.org directly.
Lightning readiness is reported by the merchant — it may be outdated or self-reported.
MotoPass does not verify BTC Map data — it is an open-data integration, not a curated list.
Saved merchants are stored locally until Nostr sync ships — switching devices loses the list.
CSV exports are snapshots — they do not update automatically as merchants change on BTC Map.

member_scripts.what_is_btcmap: BTC Map is like Yelp but for Bitcoin: a community-maintained map of businesses that accept Bitcoin, created and verified by users worldwide.
member_scripts.how_many_merchants: MotoPass shows the number of Bitcoin-accepting merchants near each program's capital city. The density badge tells you at a glance whether there's a strong Bitcoin commerce scene.
member_scripts.is_it_accurate: BTC Map is community-sourced, so it may lag behind real-world changes. If you know a venue that accepts Bitcoin but isn't on the map, you can add it at btcmap.org/add-location.
member_scripts.what_is_density: Density is the number of Bitcoin-accepting merchants within a radius of the program's capital. Sparse means few options, moderate means a growing scene, dense means plenty of places to spend Bitcoin.
member_scripts.can_i_save_merchants: Yes — sign in with a Nostr extension and click the heart icon on any merchant. Your saved list is stored locally and will sync across devices when Nostr relay sync ships.
member_scripts.how_do_i_export: Click the CSV download button in the merchant directory. You get a spreadsheet with name, address, coordinates, and verification date for every merchant in the current filter.
member_scripts.what_is_lightning: Lightning-ready means the merchant accepts Bitcoin Lightning Network payments — near-instant, near-zero-fee transactions. Look for the ⚡ badge on the map.
member_scripts.how_do_i_add_venue: Click 'Report Venue' on the BTC Map page — it links to btcmap.org/add-location with the coordinates pre-filled. The community verifies new submissions.
